tip.title: si + imparfait → conditionnel
tip.body: To imagine something, French uses si + imparfait in the 'if' part and the conditional in the result: Si j'avais plus de temps, je voyagerais davantage. Never put the conditional right after si. The conditional endings sound like the imparfait (-ais, -ait = 'è'): je voyagerais, ce serait. In careful speech the future je voyagerai ends in a closed 'é' and the conditional je voyagerais in an open 'è', but many speakers barely distinguish them, so context does the work. In fast speech j'aimerais has three syllables: 'jèm-rè'.

lessons.title: Advice and polite requests
lessons.goal: Give advice and ask for things politely with the conditional.

tip.title: tu devrais, à ta place, pourriez-vous
tip.body: The conditional softens everything. Advice: Tu devrais… (you should), À ta place, je… / Si j'étais toi, je… (if I were you), Il vaudrait mieux + infinitive (it would be better to). Requests: Pourriez-vous… ? / Tu pourrais… ? (could you), Ça vous dérangerait de… ? (would you mind). Pronunciation: pourriez has a double r but you say a single r: 'pou-rié'; the final s of devrais is silent: 'de-vrè'.

tip.title: Countries, cities and your dream home
tip.body: Use à for cities (à Montréal, à Genève, à Dakar), en for feminine countries and regions (en Suisse, en Belgique), au for masculine ones (au Québec, au Canada, au Sénégal). Describe an imaginary home with the conditional of avoir: Ma maison idéale aurait un jardin. Préférer A à B means to prefer A to B. Note the liaison in les_États-Unis (aux_États-Unis): 'o-zé-ta-zu-ni'.

lessons.title: The conditional and si-clauses
lessons.goal: Form the conditional and build si + imparfait sentences.

tip.title: Future stem + imparfait endings
tip.body: The conditional = the future stem (usually the infinitive; -re verbs drop the e: prendre → prendr-) + the imparfait endings -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient: je parlerais, nous prendrions. Irregular stems are the same as in the future: être → ser-, avoir → aur-, aller → ir-, faire → fer-, pouvoir → pourr-, vouloir → voudr-, devoir → devr-, venir → viendr-, savoir → saur-. In a hypothesis: si + imparfait, then conditional — never the conditional after si. The two halves can swap: Je partirais si je pouvais. Si becomes s' only before il/ils (s'il), never before elle.

story.title: Partir à Montréal
story.intro: Léa, a nurse from Lyon, tells her Québécoise friend Geneviève that she's thinking of moving to Montreal.

lines.name: Léa
lines.t: Geneviève, je pense à partir vivre au Québec. Qu'est-ce que tu en penses ?

lines.n: That would be quite an adventure! Where would you go? Montreal?

lines.n: Yes. I'm a nurse, and apparently they're hiring a lot over there.

lessons.title: A year anywhere

culture.title: Living in French — beyond France
culture.body: Many French people dream of a life elsewhere, and French opens far more doors than France alone. Montreal is one of the largest French-speaking cities in the world, and Québec actively recruits French-speaking workers; young French people often go there on a working holiday visa (the PVT, programme vacances-travail). In Switzerland, French is spoken in the west of the country (Geneva, Vaud, Neuchâtel, Jura and parts of Fribourg and Valais); in Belgium, in Wallonia and in bilingual Brussels. In West Africa, French is an official language in countries such as Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire, alongside local languages like Wolof.
